records.head: core_promise_weakened
records.where: bars.json B4 (accept[0], meant.intent, range); definition.md 'Implementation choices' exposure proxy; models.md M3
records.evidence: Owner-ratified sheet design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/sleeping_ice.md:180-183: "Gameplay: your heating is your threat generator. Insulate, run cold, and nothing comes. Heat the base to a comfortable temperature and you have lit a flare on a dark plain. That is a real strategic tension". B4 accept[0] instead accepts "A warm refuge retains its indoor comfort after its exterior is better insulated; the readout falls", and its meant.intent says "insulation preserves useful warmth indoors". definition.md weights a closed door at 0.25, a wall face at 0.1/t and a roof cell at 0.05 against 1 for an open boundary. On those coefficients a walled, roofed, closed-door room is weighted at well under a tenth of an exposed one [guess ~85%, arithmetic on a 5x5 room]. B4, B8 and M3 compare only exposed against insulated rooms at equal comfort. None of them requires that a comfortably heated insulated base still draws more breach pressure than the same insulated base run cold. So the comfort-against-safety tension the owner ratified can be insulated away and no bar would refuse it.
records.would_pass: A B4 pair that keeps both owner clauses: insulation lowers pressure, but a comfortable insulated refuge still draws more breach pressure than the same refuge run cold. M3 must check that ordering, not only the open-against-closed one.
records.smallest_fix: Add a B4 reject picture: "A walled, roofed base heated to comfort draws breaches no more often than the same base left cold." Add a 'comfortable insulated vs cold insulated, same walls' paired cohort to B4.range and to M3's sweep and calibration. Reword meant.intent to cite sleeping_ice.md §4 'comfortable = flare' alongside 'insulate'.

records.head: extra_without_argument
records.where: census.json row tellurox_livestock (fate life); bars.json B2 accept[0] and reject[0]
records.evidence: The row says "Housed in this module, not on its inline wild roster" and gives as its why only "Imported working livestock carries cargo and yields permanent shell when butchered; it is not a new wild admission." Its needed_by is empty. Its home was a tier migration by card (OWNER.jsonl tsn 1792859729611947407, byCard "Tellurox home → RM tier, lore removed"), not a ruling that it is this biome's life. A player meets it only through trade. It carries its own permanent-shell butcher bonus. Even so, B2 makes it part of passing ("an imported tellurox carries cargo"; reject "the shell pack beast cannot carry a caravan load").
records.would_pass: Either a stated deletion argument showing why land, life or the signature fails without tellurox, or tellurox classed as a def the module hosts (a dependency or outside the biome's first-version life), with B2's pack picture met by any imported pack animal.
records.smallest_fix: Change tellurox_livestock's fate to dependency (a hosted def, kept as is), and rewrite B2's pictures to say "an imported pack animal carries cargo" instead of naming tellurox and its shell.

records.head: evidence_cannot_tell
records.evidence: B2 says "A colony on the ice must bring food" and rejects "renewing wild pasture". The proposal keeps every visitor admission at positive density (census ice_doctrine "Density 0.2"; surface_roster: zhissa inline, plus RSW_CaveLemming, RSW_Wampa and RSW_Tauntaun patched in), and the vanilla wild spawner keeps topping that population up. B2.range lists "fed/unfed imported livestock, birth, milking, caravan loading, casualty and ordinary departure". B2.control only "distinguish[es] milk from hidden grazing". No branch hunts the visitors. A camp living indefinitely on hunted, respawning visitors would pass every observation B2 makes while breaking its 'must bring food' sentence.
records.would_pass: B2's range and control include a hunting branch over the respawning visitors, and B2 says plainly whether hunting scarce visitors is allowed as a supplement or must fail to sustain a camp.
records.smallest_fix: Add 'hunting admitted visitors across days 1–15 at shipped density' to B2.range, add a food-provenance control that tags meat by hunted pawn, and add one accept or reject picture that settles whether hunting visitors can feed the camp.

records.head: reads_with_mechanic_off
records.where: bars.json B1 sees.on and range.left_out; definition.md 'Using it' (Deeps host required)
records.evidence: definition.md: "The first version requires SleepingIce to host a working Lantern Deeps descent and return at shipped defaults in both franchise-free and campaign loads." sleeping_ice.md §6 allows exactly one surface glow: "Lantern Deeps emergences ... leak the caverns' glow at the surface; they are not residents." B1 says "without ... a native surface glow", yet its sees.on lists CreatureBehaviors, Wreckage, EnvironmentalHazards, ExplosiveGrowth, Bones and WeatherSuite, and leaves Lantern Deeps out (only B8.on loads it). B1 can therefore pass its land and glow judgement on maps where the required neighbour's entrance scatter and glow cannot appear.
records.would_pass: B1's scene loads Lantern Deeps at shipped defaults, includes entrance-present and entrance-absent cohorts, and has a picture that tells the allowed emergence leak apart from a native glow.
records.smallest_fix: Append "Lantern Deeps at shipped defaults (entrance-present and no-entrance cohorts)" to B1.sees.on and B1.range.varies, and add a reject picture: "glow spreads across the ice away from any Deeps emergence".

records.head: figurative_unmarked
records.evidence: B4 says "A camp that exposes more warmth to the ice draws greater breach pressure". 'Breach pressure' is the dial and breach-chance sensor, not physical ice pressure: definition.md says "Heat pressure is a sensor of exposure, not a second temperature". 'Exposes ... to the ice' means the exterior-transmission proxy, not heat reaching ice cells. figurative is [] and no accept picture departs from the literal reading.
records.would_pass: meant.figurative names 'breach pressure' (the continuous thermal dial and the breach chance it drives) and 'exposes warmth to the ice' (the outdoor exposure the proxy counts), each with an accept picture that departs from the literal reading.
records.smallest_fix: Add the two figurative entries and one accept picture: "No ice cell warms and nothing deforms, yet the thermal readout rises and breaches follow when a warm room's door is left open."

fixes.changed: B4 requires insulation to lower breach pressure at equal comfort and the same insulated refuge to draw more breaches at comfort than when run cold. Its pictures and controls test both comparisons. The exposure rule and M3 require the ordering under shipped event gates with legal ice and free capacity.

fixes.changed: Marked breach pressure and exposure to the ice as figurative and gave both the open-door picture where the readout and breach frequency rise without the ice warming or deforming.

R1.evidence: bars.json B4 now keeps both clauses. meant.intent reads "sleeping_ice.md §4 pairs insulation and cold operation with the warning that heating to comfort lights a flare ... a comfortable insulated refuge still draws more breach pressure than that same refuge run cold." accept[0] adds "With the same insulation, running the refuge cold lowers the readout and breach frequency further." The new reject[2] is the suggested picture: "a walled, roofed refuge heated to comfort draws breaches no more often than the same insulated refuge run cold." range.varies adds "pair a comfortably heated insulated refuge with the same insulated refuge run cold, holding walls, roof, closed doors, floor and legal bare-ice perimeter fixed, with free shivven capacity." sees.control varies heater duty "from comfort to a stabilized cold state" with the enclosure held fixed. models.md M3's Question now asks for the full ordering "exposed warm to insulated warm to the same insulated refuge run cold". Its sweep adds the paired warm/cold runs of one insulated refuge. Its calibration requires "lower dial readings and fewer natural openings in the cold cohort" and says "A tie in openings because both states stay below the dial threshold fails". definition.md (Implementation choices) adds the same rule: "If both insulated states stay below the event threshold, the comparison fails even if the dial moves." This closes the insulate-it-away false pass the record named.

R2.evidence: census.json tellurox_livestock now has "fate": "dependency", serves "Hosted livestock and shell definitions used by ordinary trade, caravans and butchery", and why "The tier move establishes their home. Any imported pack animal can satisfy the biome's cargo picture." bars.json B2 accept[0] now reads "an imported pack animal carries cargo". reject[0] reads "an imported pack animal cannot carry a caravan load". Neither names tellurox or its shell any more. This is the record's smallest_fix as written.

R3.evidence: bars.json B2 says now settles the question: "hunting its scarce visitors only supplements meals". accept[2] reads "A hunted visitor provides a meal, and the camp still needs brought-in food as new visitors arrive". reject[2], also used as lazy, reads "the camp stays fed on hunted visitors as the ordinary wild spawner keeps replacing them". range.varies adds "Across days 1–15, pair hunting admitted visitors at shipped density with a no-hunt control, including cohorts where the ordinary spawner replenishes hunted visitors." sees.control starts those cohorts with "empty food stores" and excludes other food. It keeps "the ordinary wild spawner running", tags "meat by hunted pawn through butchery, cooking and consumption", and tracks nutrition to see "whether hunting alone meets ongoing needs." A camp living on respawning visitors would now be refused.

R4.evidence: bars.json B1 sees.on now ends "Lantern Deeps at shipped defaults in both entrance-present and no-entrance cohorts." range.varies adds "Include ordinary Lantern Deeps entrance-present and no-entrance cohorts at shipped defaults in franchise-free and campaign loads." accept[2] reads "A Lantern Deeps emergence leaks a local glow at its opening while the surrounding ice remains under the cold sky light". reject[2] reads "The ice gives off its own glow away from any Lantern Deeps emergence." sees.control adds "Compare glow at the placed Deeps emergence, away from it and on no-entrance maps under matched sky and lamp conditions." The scene now loads the required neighbour, and the pictures separate the allowed leak from a native glow.

R5.evidence: bars.json B4 meant.figurative now holds two entries. The first is "breach pressure": "The continuous thermal dial and the chance of a breach it drives when an opening is eligible." The second is "exposes more warmth to the ice": "The exterior-transmission proxy counts more outdoor exposure from a warm source." Each carries the accept picture "With a warm room's door left open, no ice cell warms or deforms, yet the thermal readout rises and breaches become more frequent across matched, eligible camps." That picture is also added as accept[2]. It departs from the literal reading of both phrases. Sharing one picture between the two entries meets would_pass, because it departs from both.
